title: Tracing 3D Anatomy in 2D Strokes: Can Projection-Derived Masks Replace 3D Segmentation for Cervical Spine Fracture Recognition?
abstract: arXiv:2601.15235v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Cervical spine fractures require rapid and accurate diagnosis, yet automatic CT interpretation remains challenging as subtle injuries must be assessed across large 3D volumes. We ask whether full 3D vertebra segmentation is necessary for fracture recognition, or whether vertebra masks approximated from 2D projections preserve sufficient diagnostic context. In the proposed multi-stage pipeline, a YOLOv8 detector localizes the cervical spine from multi-view variance projections (3D mean Intersection over Union 94.45%). Multi-label vertebra segmentation is performed with a DenseNet121-Unet on energy-based sagittal and coronal projections (mean Dice 87.86%). The predicted 2D masks are back-projected and fused into approximate 3D masks per vertebra to extract volumes of interest from the original CT, which are analyzed by an ensemble of 2.5D spatio-sequential CNN-Transformer models. On the full RSNA 2022 cohort at native prevalence

translated_title: 在二维笔迹中勾勒三维解剖：投影衍生的掩膜能否替代三维分割用于颈椎骨折识别？
translated_abstract: 颈椎骨折需要快速且准确的诊断，然而由于微小的损伤必须在大体积三维影像中进行评估，自动CT判读仍然充满挑战。我们提出这样的问题：骨折识别是否必须进行完整的三维椎体分割，还是从二维投影近似得到的椎体掩膜即可保留足够的诊断上下文信息。在所提出的多阶段流水线中，YOLOv8检测器从多视图方差投影中定位颈椎（三维平均交并比为94.45%）。随后在基于能量的矢状面和冠状面投影上，使用DenseNet121-Unet执行多标签椎体分割（平均Dice系数为87.86%）。预测的二维掩膜被反投影并融合为每个椎体的近似三维掩膜，用于从原始CT中提取感兴趣体积，再由2.5D时空序列CNN-Transformer模型集成进行分析。在具有自然患病率的完整RSNA 2022数据集上……
tldr: 本研究提出一种多阶段流水线，通过从二维投影近似生成椎体掩膜来替代完整的三维分割，在大幅降低计算复杂度的同时，仍能保留足够的诊断上下文以实现颈椎骨折的高精度识别。
en_tdlr: This study proposes a multi-stage pipeline in which vertebra masks approximated from 2D projections can replace full 3D segmentation for cervical spine fracture recognition, substantially reducing computational complexity while preserving sufficient diagnostic context for high-accuracy detection.
